meta.title: Why Term Life Insurance Costs So Much Less Than Whole Life
meta.hook: Term and whole life can promise the same death benefit while charging dramatically different premiums because they cover different promises.
meta.description: Term life insurance only pays out if death occurs within a fixed window and builds no cash value, which is why it's priced far lower than whole life. Whole life covers you permanently and builds a cash value you can borrow against, which makes it a bundle of insurance plus a savings product — and priced accordingly. Educational content only, not financial advice.
